Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik and Hannah for the technical runbook and purge evidence.

High-level summary so you have something immediately for procurement: we provide region pinning for Dedicated pools (customer chooses region at provisioning) and we enforce tenant isolation at three layers — compute namespace, storage encryption scope (per-tenant keys where requested), and backup replication scoping. Backups for Dedicated tenants can be configured to stay in-region only; our default is cross-region replication for resiliency unless the customer requests region-only replication.

I attached the runbook that outlines the pinning and isolation controls, plus a short extraction of a recent purge job we ran for a staging tenant (logs redacted for PII). The runbook includes the verification checklist you can use during an audit.

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik can provide the wipe job ids and a brief technical note on cryptographic erasure vs object deletion (below).
- Hannah can share how control-plane metadata is handled and retention windows.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute call Thu 22 Oct 10:00 PT if that works for you to walk the package and capture any follow-ups.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Wed, 21 Oct 2026 at 09:12, Jordan Blake wrote:
> I attached the runbook that outlines the pinning and isolation controls, plus a short extraction of a recent purge job we ran for a staging tenant (logs redacted for PII).

Quick technical addendum (summary):
- Purge workflow: requests are initiated at the control plane with a tenant ID. The orchestration service schedules an in-region wipe job that has two phases: (1) logical object deletion from region-scoped storage buckets, (2) overwrite/zeroing of ephemeral caches and index shards where applicable.
- Snapshots: block snapshots are marked for deletion and a region-scoped garbage collection sweep removes underlying blocks. By default, snapshots are not replicated cross-region for pinned Dedicated pools.
- Cryptographic erasure: for tenants using customer-managed keys (CMK), we rotate and revoke the per-tenant key material and run a key-scrub audit record. This achieves practical irrecoverability for encrypted objects.

Evidence included in the attachment:
- wipe-job-id: WJ-FT-9421-20261020-88 (metadata record)
- gc-scan-id: GC-FT-9421-20261021-03 (removal sweep)
- sample log extract: shows state transitions and confirmation events (timestamps present).

Let me know if you need raw logs with an NDA — for production tenants we only provide redacted job traces unless there's an approved audit scope.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
